name: MAGIS-100
summary: A 100 m vertical atom interferometer for ultralight dark matter and tests of quantum mechanics, also validating technology for future gravitational-wave instruments.
detection_principle: Falling ultracold strontium clouds receive shared laser pulses; interference phases reveal dark-matter-induced changes in energy levels or acceleration.

status.label: Under construction
status.evidence: 2026 sources support the phase recorded here, rather than a real-time status of the entire project as of the access date.

timeline.event: Fermilab completes laser lab construction for world’s largest vertical atom interferometer

collaboration.name: MAGIS-100 Collaboration / project team
collaboration.participants_note: Only documented principal institutions are listed; full author and affiliation lists are in the sources. Collaborating-institution addresses are not substituted for detector locations.

results.summary: An official January 2026 report states that laser-laboratory construction was complete; atom-source delivery and vacuum-pipe installation remained subsequent milestones.

science_scope: Directly searches for Galactic-halo axions, axionlike particles or other ultralight dark matter. Limits depend on assumed local density, velocity distribution and coupling models; separate scanned mass intervals do not amount to exclusion of the entire range.
